author: vegasjj
body: # Reverse Proxy with Squid ## Environment An AWS EC2 instance running Ubuntu with the **squid** package installed was used to set up the reverse web proxy server for this proof of concept. Two more EC2 instances running Windows Server 2025 were deployed: - Origin server – no public IP; IIS role installed to serve a test webpage. All external requests to the test webpage must go through the reverse web proxy server. - Jump box – RDP bastion host used to manage the origin server as it lacks a public IP. Also, a personal Windows PC was used to test the reverse proxy by making requests to the origin server. ## Deployment The basic idea behind this implementation was to configure a reverse web proxy which would redirect all client requests to the http://proxy-demo:8080 URL to an origin server (not exposed to the internet) that served an IIS test webpage. Below, you can see an output showing a reverse web proxy configuration running on Ubuntu. You can set it up by [following this steps](./README.md). Note that the origin server's IP is **10.200.123.141** and the reverse web proxy should redirect requests made to the **proxy-demo** domain on **port 8080**. If you run: ```sh sudo systemctl status squid ``` You should see an output similar to: Above, you can see the reverse proxy server is listening for request on the port 8080. Next, the Windows jump box was used to make an RDP connection to the origin server (**10.200.123.141**) In the image above, you can see the origin server was configured with the IIS role so that it could serve the default webpage for testing purposes. If you need help to set up IIS, [follow this steps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/iis/web-hosting/web-server-for-shared-hosting/installing-the-web-server-role). Below, you can see the configuration of the hosts file on my personal PC. This step was necessary as the **proxy-demo** domain wasn't publicly registered so requests made to it would fail. A workaround consist in configuring the hosts file to point the **proxy-demo** domain to the reverse proxy server public IP (**3.131.34.143**). DO NOT use this solution for production environments. Also, a rule was added in the AWS security group associated with the reverse proxy server to allow incoming traffic to **port 8080**: Then, when I went to http://proxy-demo:8080 I could reach the origin server through the reverse web proxy server: If there is a problem with the reverse proxy server configuration you may receive the following error: Please let me know is you encounter this problem to schedule a troubleshooting session. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Improved clarity and formality in the forward proxy journal and README, including clearer descriptions and installation instructions. * Added comments to configuration examples for better guidance. * Introduced a new journal and README for the reverse proxy project, providing step-by-step setup instructions, configuration details, and troubleshooting tips, including screenshots and security guidance.

body:
Mainly focused on improvements to the documentation of fields on the query model, but also generally improving the OpenAPI docs at https://esgf-node.ornl.gov/esgf-1-5-bridge/docs and https://esgf-node.ornl.gov/esgf-1-5-bridge/redoc

Initial titles and descriptions are generated through Google Gemini using governing documents pulled from various authoritative sites (PCMDI, WCRP, ESG Search documentation site) and are intended as a starting point. Extra effort has gone into describing how the usage of fields has changed between CMIP phases as fields may no longer be in use, but may still be needed by historical data.

Examples were generated similarly by first looping through each field and issuing a faceted query on that field to retrieve it's values and counts. If a result for a field was empty, the query was retried with `type=File` under the assumption that the field might only be populated for `File` records (the default query is for `type=Dataset`). These results were provided to Gemini as a json file with the following prompt:

> Using the cumulative facets data, ensure that all examples in the model make sense. Then, make sure the examples represent good coverage of the possible values for each field

- [ ] Where possible, links to governing documents should be updated to DOI links in case they are ever removed from the source sites
- [ ] Several fields differ only in case or style. Neither Gemini nor I found documentation to prove otherwise so these fields were labeled as alternatives of each other. It is equally possible that only one of the alternatives was ever used, but also that the alternatives we from different MIP eras, or that none we ever used at all. These need to be delineated and updated/removed as appropriate
  - [ ] `Science Driver` vs `science driver` vs `science_driver`
    - Of these fields, only `science_driver` appears populated in our Solr index
    - Only E3SM data appears to have populated the `science_driver` field and the decision was made not to migrate that data to the Globus Index so that data is now unreachable. Does that imply that we can drop these fields?

author: branliu0
body:
When two citations are right next to each other (i.e., within BACKWARD_SEEK), the citation extraction can be wrong.

I was testing with the string `West v. Atkins, 487 U.S. 42, 54-58 (1988), Polk Cty. v. Dodson, 454 U.S. 312, 325-26 (1981), and Monell v. Department of Soc. Servs., 436 U.S. 658, 694 (1978)`

Before this fix, the second and third citations would have missing plaintiff, defendant, and pincite. Now with this small fix, those three fields are populated correctly.

I'm not super happy with this fix, but it doesn't break any tests and it'll be helpful for me. Sharing this PR here in case it's of interest or if you have better ideas for how to fix.

The main thing I'm not happy with is `word_str.endswith("),")`, which feels too tightly coupled to the specific example I have. But I'm going to move on for now and I'll come back to this when/if I find more real-life examples.

body:
Added support for Google Cloud Storage and Rclone based repos by making the repo url and rclone environment a little more configurable.

I also had to make a couple qol changes to get it running on my machine:
- using `dateutil.parser.isoparse` instead of `datetime.datetime.fromisotime`, for some reason my timestamps had too many decimals
- pulling the log level from uvicorn's logger and using that globally, so I could use `--log-level=debug`

I tried to keep the same code style without changing too much, but let me know if you want anything changed and I'm happy to oblige!

author: fujidaiti
body:
## Problem / Issue

Closes [#264](https://github.com/fujidaiti/smooth_sheets/issues/264).

Previously, overscroll gestures in sheets were not delegated to child scrollable widgets, making it impossible to implement pull-to-refresh functionality or other overscroll-driven animations like bouncing effects within sheet content.

## Solution

Added a new `delegateUnhandledOverscrollToChild` flag to `SheetScrollConfiguration` that allows unhandled overscroll deltas to be passed to child scrollables.

### Key changes
- Added `delegateUnhandledOverscrollToChild` boolean flag to `SheetScrollConfiguration` (defaults to `false`)
- Updated scroll handling logic in `_ScrollAwareSheetActivityMixin` to delegate unhandled overscroll when flag is enabled

### How it works
- When `true`, scroll deltas from overscroll gestures that aren't handled by the sheet's physics are passed to the child scrollable
- This enables overscroll-driven animations like `RefreshIndicator` and `BouncingScrollPhysics` effects
- Only effective when sheet physics doesn't handle overscroll (e.g., `ClampingSheetPhysics`)
- When `false` (default), maintains existing behavior where unhandled overscroll is ignored

The feature is backwards compatible and requires explicit opt-in via the configuration flag.

### Example

Added `tutorial/pull_to_refresh_in_sheet.dart` example:

author: midigofrank
body:
## Description

**Problem**: The credential modals were being rendered inside `<td>` elements, which violates HTML semantics and causes layout issues. Additionally, the credential tables and events were duplicated in different liveviews -  the `/credentials` page and the project settings page

**Solution Overview**:
The solution involves moving all the credential listing logic, modal state management, and event handling into a centralized component that is used in `/credentials` and project settings.

  ## Key Changes

  ### 1. Introduced `CredentialIndexComponent` (`lib/lightning_web/live/credential_live/credential_index_component.ex`)
  - This is the heart of the solution - a reusable LiveComponent that encapsulates everything that was previously duplicated across the `/credentials` page and project settings page
  - Handles all credential and OAuth client listing
  - Manages the `active_modal` state to control which modal is currently shown `(new_credential, edit_credential, delete_credential, transfer_credential, new_oauth_client, edit_oauth_client, delete_oauth_client)`
 

### 2. Standardized Modal Closing System
The main goal was that when you click Cancel or the X button on any credential modal, it should hide the modal and remove it from the DOM. This is achieved by having all modal close events target the `CredentialIndexComponent`.   

To make it easy to target the `CredentialIndexComponent`, I added  3 helper components: 
- **`Components.Credentials.credentials_index_live_component/1`**: Ensures that the livecomponent always uses the same ID.
  - **`Components.Credentials.credential_modal/1`**: A `<.modal />` wrapper. By default targets the `CredentialIndexComponent` by `id` for close events.
  - **`Components.Credentials.credential_modal_cancel_button`**: It automatically targets the `CredentialIndexComponent` by `id` when clicked.
  
Both the`credential_modal` and `credential_modal_cancel_button` have a default `on_modal_close` assign that sends `close_active_modal` events to the `CredentialIndexComponent`, but this can be overridden for special cases such as in the `Workflow edit page`.

Ensure you test all the actions, `create, edit, transfer, revoke transfer and delete`

Closes #1588

## Validation steps

This needs a lot of click testing on all the credential pages. Visit any of the `/credentials`, `project settings` or even the `workflow edit page for adding a new credential`. 

## Additional notes for the reviewer

- I have renamed `ModalPortal` to `LiveComponentPortal` for better clarity about its purpose. This component isn't used in the current PR but provides a foundation for future modal rendering improvements. The rename makes it clear that this is for rendering LiveComponents outside their normal DOM location
- Codecov has highlighted missing coverage for oauth client edit and deletion. Most of those tests were tagged with `:skip`. I have created a separate issue to track this: https://github.com/OpenFn/lightning/issues/3391

## Summary by Sourcery

Add cross-platform support (macOS and Linux/Flatpak) with enhanced resource handling and logging, integrate a modular intent–action system and factual consistency verification, and update build/CI pipelines to produce Windows, macOS (Intel/ARM), Linux executables and artifacts.

New Features:
- Add macOS SSL certificate installation and PortAudio support for macOS builds
- Introduce Linux and Flatpak support with lockfile instance management and shared data directories
- Implement Low Memory Mode to offload models on resource-constrained systems

Enhancements:

- Optimize on-demand loading/unloading of Whisper STT models per platform

Build:
- Update GitHub Actions to build and upload Windows installers, macOS Intel/ARM PKG, and Linux Flatpak bundles
- Add platform-specific build scripts for PyInstaller (build-mac.sh, build-pkg.sh, build-linux.sh) and FlatpakManifest

CI:
- Extend release workflow to package and publish multi-OS artifacts
- Add CI steps for Mac and Linux installer generation

Documentation:
- Improve help documentation to clarify context window setting units

Tests:
- Add unit tests for settings type conversion, intent recognizers, action handlers, and factual consistency verifier

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The sample projects in the `Samples/` directory were failing to build on GitHub's Linux runners due to two main issues:

1. **Missing .NET Framework targeting packs**: Projects were targeting .NET Framework 4.6.2, which requires Windows-specific targeting packs not available on Linux build agents
2. **packages.config format**: Using the legacy packages.config format instead of PackageReference, which causes NuGet restore issues with `dotnet` CLI on non-Windows platforms

```
error MSB3644: The reference assemblies for .NETFramework,Version=v4.6.2 were not found. To resolve this, install the Developer Pack (SDK/Targeting Pack) for this framework version or retarget your application.
```

## Solution

Migrated all three sample projects to modern SDK-style project format:

### Key Changes
- **Project Format**: Converted from old-style .csproj to SDK-style project format with `<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">`
- **Target Framework**: Upgraded from .NET Framework 4.6.2 to 4.8 for better cross-platform build support
- **Package Management**: Replaced `packages.config` files with `<PackageReference>` entries directly in project files
- **Assembly Merging**: Made ILRepack functionality conditional (`Condition="'$(OS)' == 'Windows_NT'"`) to support cross-platform builds

### Projects Updated
- `Samples/BusinessDomain/BusinessDomain.csproj`
- `Samples/SamplePlugins/SamplePlugins.csproj` 
- `Samples/SamplePlugins2/SamplePlugins2.csproj`

### Cross-Platform Considerations
- **Linux/macOS**: Sample projects build successfully without assembly merging
- **Windows**: Full functionality maintained including ILRepack assembly merging
- **Package Compatibility**: All Dataverse SDK packages work correctly with .NET Framework 4.8

## Verification

- ✅ Complete solution builds successfully on Linux (`dotnet build`)
- ✅ All existing tests continue to pass (`dotnet test`)
- ✅ Clean build from scratch works correctly (`dotnet clean && dotnet build`)
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality

Fixes #1.

This PR introduces a fully functional **Radio Player Page** and **Recordings Page** to the RA App, aligning with the Figma design. Key updates include:

## 🎧 Features
- Implement new **Radio Player Page** with reusable `PlayerInfo` widget.
- Add **Recordings Page** populated with interactive widgets.

- Fix recording fetching bug - skip faulty/empty recordings without breaking the page.
- Add debug-mode error logging for easier troubleshooting.
- Refactor `RaPageTemplate` for better readability and maintainability.
- Standardize fonts and layout styling to match Figma specs.
- Upgrade Flutter and resolve related linter issues.

## 🔗 Integration & Embeds
- Integrate support for embed content.

- #94

author: marcelo-alvarez
body:
## Overview

This PR introduces a pipeline for generating mock galaxy catalogs from AbacusSummit halo catalogs using the `rgrspit_diffsky` package. The pipeline is designed to support large-scale covariance mock generation for the Roman Galactic Redshift Survey (GRS) Project Infrastructure Team (PIT) analysis.

## Changes

### Features

- **Mock Generation Pipeline**: Rudimentary script for generating a galaxy catalog from halo data
- **Environment Setup**: Environment loading with module and conda configuration
- **Visualization**: Simple dual-panel scatter plot with zoom insets
- **Parallelization**: MPI / distributed JAX support with slab decomposition

### Files Added

- `scripts/load_env.sh` - Environment setup script for NERSC Perlmutter
- `scripts/make_mocks.sh` - Main pipeline orchestration script with CLI options
- `scripts/make_sfh_cov_mocks.py` - Core mock generation with star formation history modeling
- `scripts/plot_mock_catalog.py` - Visualization script for galaxy and halo distributions
- `examples/halo_galaxy_scatter_*.png` - Example output visualization

### Documentation

- **README**: Updated with basic instructions, overview, and examples

## Key Features

### Pipeline
- **Input**: AbacusSummit halo catalogs (500 Mpc/h small box)
- **Galaxy Model**: Star formation history modeling via `rgrspit_diffsky`
- **Output**: HDF5 catalogs with galaxy positions, masses, and properties
- **Scaling**: Designed for 40,000+ catalog generation runs

### Parallelization
- **MPI Parallelization**: Scales across multiple GPUs/nodes
- **Parallel HDF5**: Collective I/O operations with h5py
- **Domain Decomposition**: Simplified slab decomposition

## Output

The pipeline generates:
- **Galaxy Catalogs**: HDF5 files with positions, masses, and properties
- **Visualizations**: Two-panel scatter plots with halo/galaxy distributions and zoom insets
- **Logs**: Detailed execution logs for monitoring and debugging

## Testing

- Test mode validated with 5,000 halo subset
- MPI scaling tested across multiple GPU nodes
- Visualization pipeline verified with example output
- Environment setup tested on NERSC Perlmutter

## Dependencies

- NERSC Perlmutter environment
- Conda environment with JAX, CUDA-aware mpi4py, and `rgrspit_diffsky`

## Next steps
- Refactor monolithic scripts into more maintainable modular structure
- Validation of single mock galaxy catalog at z=1.1
- Add Slurm orchestration of multiple realizations in a single campaign for a given galaxy formation model in `rgrspit_diffsky` with appropriate versioning and tagging

author: rishixkumar
body:
Overview

This PR introduces the foundational authentication system for the Spectra platform, establishing secure user registration, login, and stateless session management using JWTs. The implementation is central to enabling all user-specific features and is a core milestone for the MVP.

Key Features and Technical Decisions

  • User Registration Endpoint
    • Added /users/register endpoint to allow new users to sign up with email and password.
    • Passwords are hashed using passlib[bcrypt] before storage, ensuring that no plain text credentials are ever persisted.
    • Duplicate email prevention is enforced at the API level, returning a clear error if an email is already registered.
    • Technical Issue: During setup, a persistent "role does not exist" error was encountered. Investigation revealed that both a local Postgres instance (managed by Homebrew) and the Dockerized Postgres were running on port 5432, causing FastAPI to connect to the wrong database. Stopping the Homebrew-managed service and ensuring only the Docker instance was active resolved the issue. This highlighted the importance of monitoring port conflicts and background service managers when using Docker for development.
  • User Login and JWT Token Issuance
    • Implemented /users/login endpoint, authenticating users via email and password using OAuth2 standards.
    • On successful authentication, the system generates a signed JWT access token with python-jose, enabling stateless authentication for future requests.
    • Password verification is handled securely with bcrypt, preventing exposure of sensitive data even in the event of a database breach.
    • Technical Considerations: JWT implementation required careful handling of secret keys and token expiration. The secret is kept out of version control, and token expiry is set to balance security and usability. This approach lays the groundwork for scalable, secure session management.
  • Additional Features
    • Structured the backend using modular directories (models/, schemas/, core/, routers/) to support future scalability and maintainability.
    • Introduced SQLAlchemy models for the user table and Pydantic schemas for input/output validation.
    • Created CRUD utilities for user creation, retrieval, and password verification.
    • Configured database session management using dependency injection for reliable DB access.
    • Updated requirements.txt to include all necessary security and ORM libraries.

Problems Encountered and Solutions

  • Database Connectivity: The primary challenge was resolving port conflicts between local and Dockerized Postgres instances. The solution involved stopping the Homebrew-managed Postgres service and ensuring Docker's instance was the only one running on port 5432.
  • Password Security: Implemented and tested bcrypt hashing to ensure passwords are never stored in plain text and that verification is robust against edge cases.
  • JWT Management: Ensured that JWT token creation uses strong secrets and appropriate expiration, with code structured for easy secret rotation in production environments.

Files Added/Modified

  • app/routers/user.py – Registration and login endpoints
  • app/schemas/user.py – User input/output schemas
  • app/models/user.py – User database model
  • app/core/crud_user.py – CRUD logic and password verification
  • app/core/jwt.py – JWT utility functions
  • app/core/database.py – Database session management
  • requirements.txt – Added security and ORM dependencies

Testing and Validation

  • Registration and login endpoints tested via FastAPI Swagger UI (/docs).
  • Verified hashed password storage and duplicate email handling.
  • Confirmed JWT token structure and expiry.

Next Steps

  • Merge this branch into main to complete the authentication foundation for Spectra.
  • Proceed with implementing protected routes, user profile endpoints, and frontend authentication integration.

author: luisandres248
body:
…ción

He implementado un componente gráfico avanzado para la visualización y análisis de señales de audio en Flutter, cumpliendo con la especificación técnica que me proporcionaste.

Características Principales:
- Muestra la forma de onda (amplitud vs. tiempo) de archivos WAV y MP3.
- Compatible con Flutter Web y Android (decodificación y reproducción).
- Conversión automática de audio estéreo a mono.
- El gráfico muestra la señal de audio completa por defecto, ajustándose al ancho disponible.
- Eje X representa el tiempo (segundos), Eje Y representa la amplitud normalizada (-1.0 a 1.0).
- Barra vertical roja indica el punto actual de reproducción, se mueve automáticamente y es interactiva (clic para buscar).
- Downsampling dinámico para manejar eficientemente audios largos (probado hasta 30 min en concepto).
- He implementado la funcionalidad opcional de mostrar marcas de picos detectados en el gráfico.

Componentes Modificados y Creados:
- `AudioDecoderService`: Lo he refactorizado para decodificación multiplataforma (Web: AudioContext, Móvil: wav_io para WAV, flutter_sound para MP3). Normaliza y convierte a mono.
- `AudioPlayerService`: He creado un nuevo servicio para manejar la reproducción de audio (play, pause, seek, stop, carga desde bytes) usando `flutter_sound`. Proporciona streams para el estado y la posición.
- `AudioVisualizer`: Lo he mejorado significativamente:
    - Eje X dinámico basado en la duración total del audio.
    - Downsampling adaptable al ancho del widget.
    - Eje Y normalizado.
    - Barra de progreso vertical interactiva.
    - Marcas de picos opcionales.
- `AppState`: Integra los nuevos servicios, gestiona el estado del audio y la reproducción, y provee los datos a la UI.
- `AudioData`: He actualizado el modelo para incluir timestamps de picos y sampleRate.
- `AudioAnalysisService`: Lo he corregido para usar el sampleRate correcto y devolver timestamps de picos.

Consideraciones:
- La funcionalidad de zoom/scroll horizontal se consideró opcional y no la he implementado en esta iteración.
- He realizado pruebas lógicas y revisiones de código exhaustivas. Te recomiendo la prueba en dispositivos/emuladores reales para verificar todos los aspectos de permisos, rendimiento y comportamiento específico de la plataforma.

# PR Approval Steps

## For Requester

1. Description
    - [ ] Check the PR title and description for clarity. It should describe the changes made and the reason behind them.
    - [ ] Ensure that the PR follows the contribution guidelines, if applicable.
2. Security requirements
    - [ ] Ensure that a Pull Request (PR) does not expose passwords and other sensitive information by using git-secrets and upload relevant evidence: https://github.com/awslabs/git-secrets
    - [ ] Ensure commit has GitHub Commit Signature
3. Manual review
    1. Click on the Files changed tab to see the code changes. Review the changes thoroughly:
        - [ ] Code Quality: Check for coding standards, naming conventions, and readability.
        - [ ] Functionality: Ensure that the changes meet the requirements and that all necessary code paths are tested.
        - [ ] Security: Check for any security issues or vulnerabilities.
        - [ ] Documentation: Confirm that any necessary documentation (code comments, README updates, etc.) has been updated.
4. Check for Merge Conflicts:
    - [ ] Verify if there are any merge conflicts with the base branch. GitHub will usually highlight this. If there are conflicts, you should resolve them.
      
## For Reviewer

1. Go through `For Requester` section to double check each item.
2. Request Changes or Approve the PR:
    1. If the PR is ready to be merged, click Review changes and select Approve.
    2. If changes are required, select Request changes and provide feedback. Be constructive and clear in your feedback.
3. Merging the PR
    1. Check the Merge Method:
        1. Decide on the appropriate merge method based on your repository's guidelines (e.g., Squash and merge, Rebase and merge, or Merge).
    2. Merge the PR:
        1. Click the Merge pull request button.
        2. Confirm the merge by clicking Confirm merge.

author: lia-viam
body:
third time's the charm? this should finally fix the  _`always-rebuild`_ logic in `ReconfigureResource`, making sure that the old resource is destructed before the new one is created. this was causing issues with realsense and would cause issues for any other unique or global resource which has sole ownership of a device, socket, etc.

this adds an overload of `replace_one` which takes a construction callback, bringing the logic closer to that of eg python
https://github.com/viamrobotics/viam-python-sdk/blob/main/src/viam/module/module.py#L253

i marked the old one as deprecated for now but we may just want to remove it entirely 

cc @hexbabe @acmorrow

### Summary
This PR adds a new section to the Scaled UI Amount Integration Guide, specifically outlining the recommended integration requirements and priorities for Centralized Exchanges (CEXes) when supporting tokens that use the Scaled UI Amount extension.

### Details
* Added a requirements table for CEXes, detailing best practices and priorities for integrating tokens with the Scaled UI Amount extension.
* Requirements include tracking multiplier updates, displaying rebased token balances, supporting user actions in UiAmount, handling historical actions, tracking raw balances internally, adapting price feeds, displaying price history graphs, and scaling cost basis.
* Each requirement is assigned a priority (P0 or P1) to help CEXes prioritize their integration efforts.

body:
#### d7b590ea57cb326ed41fe380796d01f8363a50dd 
[JSC] Make JSRopeString non destructible
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=295822
rdar://155652531

Reviewed by NOBODY (OOPS!).

Previously JSRopeString was destructible since it may hold a resolved
string. This makes sweeping a bit complicated since JSRopeString is one
of the most frequently allocated cells while only up to 20% of cells are
actually having resolved strings.
This patch makes JSRopeString non destructible. When the string is
resolved, we allocate JSString as a holder and making sure that this
string is owning the resolved string. And JSRopeString is visiting this
string so that it indirectly keeps StringImpl alive. But JSRopeString
itself is not keeping String so we no longer need to call a destructor
of JSRopeString.

author: maanug-nv
body:
Changes needed to support models output by the bridge.

Case 1: With recipe and mock data (benchmarking case)
If `ModelProvider.vocab_size` is `None` , that value is copied from the tokenizer [here](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Hub/blob/c7f081bd841bd689cb5a5f46b72f4e98df9ceccd/src/megatron/hub/training/setup.py#L168). However this value is 1 greater than the vocab size provided to TokenizerConfig (see [here](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Hub/blob/c7f081bd841bd689cb5a5f46b72f4e98df9ceccd/src/megatron/hub/training/tokenizers/tokenizer.py#L1027)). This creates an issue when the vocab size **is** set in the ModelProvider, which is the case for the ModelProvider output by the bridge. In that case, the model vocab size is 1 less than the real tokenizer vocab size (including the EOD token id), so the embedding weight is short 1 row. Rather than adding a special case for this scenario (bridge model and NullTokenizer), it seems simpler to modify the NullTokenizer. We can simply let the last index be the EOD token instead of appending it. Since the NullTokenizer is only used with mock data, it shouldn't impact text generation.

Case 2: With real tokenizer configured by user
In this case, it makes sense to let the user decide which takes priority, so we can simply make an assertion. If they want the model vocab size to take priority, it should be copied to the tokenizer config. To let tokenizer vocab size take priority, they can just set model vocab size to `None`.

This pull request introduces functionality to publish user messages received via Telegram to Google Cloud Pub/Sub, along with improvements to timezone handling and code organization. The most important changes include adding a new `PubSubPublisher` class, integrating Pub/Sub publishing in the `echo` function, and reorganizing imports in `main.py`.

### Pub/Sub Integration:

* **New `PubSubPublisher` class**: Added `pubsub.py` to encapsulate Google Cloud Pub/Sub publishing logic, including initialization and message publishing with proper logging and error handling. (`[pubsub.pyR1-R36](diffhunk://#diff-1b02009a43a42ce003d72991ae8d550083b160ef59558260ccd11085ba97fc79R1-R36)`)

  - Integrated Ant Design library, with a custom theme applied via ConfigProvider (deep purples, indigos, gold accents, 'Cinzel Decorative' & 'Montserrat' fonts).
  - Refactored Header (AntD Menu), CallToActionButton (AntD Button with confetti), Footer, and placeholder page buttons to use themed AntD components.
  - Ensured high contrast for buttons and interactive elements against dark/gradient backgrounds.

- **Firebase Firestore Integration - Cosmic Messages:**
  - Implemented CosmicMessageForm.jsx for you to submit messages.
  - Implemented CosmicMessagesList.jsx to display messages from Firestore in real-time with AntD Cards.
  - Created CosmicPortalPage.jsx to host the form and list.
  - Updated navigation (Header, OracleApp routes) to include the Cosmic Portal.
  - Configured firebase.js for Firestore (requires your credentials).

- **Animations & UX:**
  - Implemented page transition animations (fade & slide) using Framer Motion (AnimatePresence, motion.div).
  - Added entry animations for key components (Header, Footer, HomePageContent, CallToActionButton).
  - Maintained interactive hover/click effects.

- **Bug Fix - `useLocation()` Error:**
  - Resolved the 'useLocation() may be used only in the context of a <Router> component' error by refactoring OracleApp.jsx.
  - Moved BrowserRouter to main.jsx to correctly wrap the application.
  - Created an `AnimatedRoutes` component within OracleApp.jsx to properly scope `useLocation` for `AnimatePresence` and `Routes`.

- **Code Quality & Structure:**
  - Added extensive JSDoc-style comments to new and refactored components.
  - Organized components into logical folders (layout, common, home, firebase, pages/placeholders).
  - Ensured the project is lint-free.

The application now provides a more engaging, aesthetically pleasing, and interactive user experience, with a solid foundation for future feature development.

body:
-> Criados mais checks para garantir que docenteTurmas seja criado no localStorage.


-> Bug não aparecia em todas as execuções (dependia da velocidade de fetch do json x troca de página na aba de login), então apesar de não ter ocorrido nenhuma vez nos testes que fiz, seria bom continuar averiguando sempre que possível (até para o possível incremento na quantidade de checks, em outras abas).

-> Esses "checks" que digo consistem na utilização da função "getDocenteTurmas" (presente em script/buscarDados.js) ao invés de simplesmente olhar no localStorage, pois a função automaticamente retorna docenteTurmas, se existir no localStorage; ou cria docenteTurmas no localStorage e retorna , se não existir.

*getDocenteTurmas é uma edição do getDocenteDisciplinas na versão atual do repositório principal. A diferença é que salva o turmaID das turmas e não somente o código da disciplina, para diferenciar turmas de mesma disciplina. Não foram achados erros na edição dessa função com outras funcionalidades.

`_map` 을 `map` 으로 이름 바꾸기

불필요한 형 변환 제거 `(HashMap<?, ?>), Integer.parseInt((String) map.get("resultCnt"))`

src/main/java/egovframework/com/sym/log/lgm/web/EgovSysLogController.java:74:	LocalVariableNamingConventions:	LocalVariableNamingConventions: 'local variable' 의 변수 '_map' 이  '[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*'  로 시작함
```

```
feature/pmd/EgovSysLogController
```

3. 이클립스 > Source > Format

```java
 *   2025.07.12  이백행          2025년 컨트리뷰션 PMD로 소프트웨어 보안약점 진단하고 제거하기-LocalVariableNamingConventions(final이 아닌 변수는 밑줄을 포함할 수 없음)

## Description

Adds CommonJS build support alongside existing ES module support, enabling the library to work in both CommonJS and ES module environments while maintaining full backward compatibility. This enhancement allows the library to be used in a wider range of Node.js environments and build systems

The changes include:
- Added `"require"` export and updated `"main"` entry point in package.json
- Added `build:cjs` and `build:all` scripts for CommonJS compilation
- Created `tsconfig.cjs.json` for CommonJS TypeScript configuration
- Added `dist-cjs/package.json` with `"type": "commonjs"` for proper module resolution
- Moved `index.ts` to `src/index.ts` for better code organization

Big fan of the project and would love to see it succeed! The dual module support will make the library more accessible to different development environments and build systems.

author: keiji
body:
Add test for Keiji device integrity certificate parsing

This commit introduces a new test case to `test_attestation_parser.py` for parsing a specific Base64 encoded certificate (`beta keiji/android-device-integrity`).

The test covers:
- Decoding the certificate.
- Loading it using the cryptography library.
- Parsing the attestation extension using `get_attestation_extension_properties`.
- Asserting top-level, software-enforced (including AttestationApplicationId), and hardware-enforced (including RootOfTrust) properties against expected values derived from the certificate.

author: justinmc
body:
This PR makes platform views ignore pointer events when they're not laid out.

Platform views register themselves for global pointer events when their RenderBox attaches:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/9c626d9f9afa6da96433e3bfc4895492f87e0009/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/platform_view.dart#L370-L380

But a RenderBox that is attached is not necessarily laid out. The problem in the issue seemed to be that a page was created offscreen (attached and not laid out), but it still received pointer events, and this caused errors with using `size` before layout.

This PR simply ignores pointer events when not laid out.

Fixes https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/83481
